lines: I watched it drag her off and I just stood there.
I should've been the one who got grabbed, not her.
She owed me three bucks and now I'll never get it back.
Stop looking at me like that, I'm fine. I'm not fine.
Okay, I'm not crying, my eyes are just dusty down here.
I keep reaching to tap her shoulder like she's still beside me.
Who thought splitting up was a good idea? Oh, right. Me.
I told her to take the left hall. That's on me.
I'm so angry I could punch a wall, and my hand already hurts.
We are going back for her. Don't argue with me about it.
Okay, deep breath. Where did it drag her? Think.
Going back in alone is stupid, so you're coming with me.
If we rush in again we'll just lose someone else too.
Let's be smart this time. Slow, quiet, and together.
I'm not waiting here while she's out there. Let's move.
I'm going back for her, even if it's dumb.
Tell me we can still get her back. Please, just say it.
I froze when it mattered. I'm not doing that again.
Her flashlight's still on the floor. Somebody grab it, please.
Who's got the last stim pack? Keep it for whoever's next.
Don't be a hero now, okay? We already lost one today.
Not gonna lie, I want to smash something right now.
I hate that I laughed at her jokes so much. Now it's quiet.
She always ate my last granola bar, the thief. I miss her already.
I'm still holding her spare batteries like an idiot.
Her voice is still in my head, yelling at me to hurry up.
My hands won't stop shaking. Give me a second, please.
I can't feel my fingers from gripping this pipe so hard.
The taser's almost dead, and I'm almost out of patience.
That thing better hope I never get close to it again.
Every time I blink I see that long arm pulling her in.
I don't care how dark it gets, we're bringing her home.
Keep your light on me, okay? I'm really scared right now.
Honestly, I'm terrified, and I'd rather you admit it too.
I'm scared of going back, but leaving her is worse.
Careful, the floor's soft here. Step where I step.
Okay, low voices, we don't know if it's still nearby.
Wait, did you hear that? Quiet for a sec, please.
I don't trust these lights. They keep blinking like they're mocking us.
Stay behind me and don't make any noise, got it?
Let's check the vents on the way, just in case she's up there.
The stairwell's clear, but I'd still rather take the long way.
Feel the wall as you go, that corner's a bad one.
If you hear me shout, drop everything and run back here.
Two of us go in, one stays by the door. That's the rule now.
Somebody watch our backs while I check the lockers.
I'll keep watch. You get the flashlight and stay close.
No heroics, no stupid plans. We get in, we get out, we get her.
I'm scared I'll make it worse. Help me not do that.
You're not allowed to blame yourself either, okay? We both messed up.
This is nobody's fault, but it still feels like mine.
I keep replaying it, and every time I'd have done something different.
She'd tell me to stop moping and get moving, so fine.
She'd be so annoyed I'm sitting here feeling sorry for myself.
I'm not giving up on her. Not today, not ever.
Tell her family we tried, if it comes to that.
Crying won't get her back, but I'm allowed one minute.
Okay, that's enough crying. Eyes up, we've got work to do.
I think I'm going to be sick. Give me one second.
We bring her back or we don't leave, that's my final word.
I'm not going to pretend I'm okay. I'm really not.
Hey, look at me. When we find her, you hug her first.
I'll miss her lousy puns every single day, honestly.
She once tried to cook us dinner from a vending machine. Terrible.
Her laugh was the only thing keeping me sane down here.
You know what's worst? She'd be fine if I'd listened.
I hope she's still alive, still grumbling about everything.
Stop asking if I'm okay, I'm trying to think here.
Fine, I'll go first, but if I scream, you run.
She'd call us idiots for even thinking about going back.
We're idiots for going back, and I'm coming anyway.
I'll check the stairs, you check behind the broken door.
Flashlight on, and no more splitting up. Promise me.
If we see that thing, we run first and wonder later.
Remember how she sang off-key? I'd give anything to hear it.
